subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Call the shots

options.text: To be a follower that makes less important decision
To be in a position to make decisions that influences a situation
To be in a powerless position that follows orders
To be in a neutral position

solution:
The correct answer is: **To be in a position to make decisions that influences a situation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom **"Call the shots"** means to be in a position of authority to make decisions that influence a situation or control an operation. (निर्णय लेने की स्थिति में होना)

 
 
• **Example: **As the director of the company, Janet always calls the shots during board meetings.
 
 
 
• **"To be in a position to make decisions that influences a situation"** accurately captures the essence of being in control or in charge, where one's decisions determine the course of actions. (निर्णय लेने की स्थिति में होना)
 
 
• **Example: **In the final stages of the project, it was clear that the project manager called the shots, guiding the team towards completion.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct meaning of **'Call the shots'** is **'To be in a position to make decisions that influences a situation'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **To be in a position to make decisions that influences a situation**.
